title: The ministers' arguments
hook: the king's ministers come to bring him home, with every argument they have (Buddhacarita 9)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Yashodhara, and a palace in mourning. Your line: the one left behind.

Your father is burning with grief. That's the opening line of the case, more or less, and it's delivered by two men who have walked a long way to say it. The king can't go himself, so he sends his family priest and his minister, with one job: bring the prince home. They find him resting under a tree. They bow. And then they begin, and they've come prepared.
screen: `TWO MEN FROM THE PALACE.` → `ONE JOB: BRING HIM HOME.` → `THEY'VE COME PREPARED.`

segments.voice: First, the heart. The priest speaks for the family: your father's grief, the queen who raised you, your wife, your small son. Come back for them. Second, the head. You can practice what is right at home, as a king. Kings of old found freedom while they still ruled. There will be time for the forest later, when you're old and the throne has passed on. Third, the doubt. The minister tries a different road. Who really knows what comes after death? Some teachers say there's another life, some say there isn't. Some say things simply happen by their own nature, the way a thorn is sharp without anyone sharpening it. Why give up everything for a question no one can settle? Love, duty, tradition, and doubt itself: they use every argument they have. Fourth, the answer. The prince hears each man out and answers each in turn. In paraphrase, he tells the priest he knows his father's love, and it grieves him, but parting will come anyway, by death if not by this. To the minister he says he won't take this question secondhand, from whichever teacher sounds surest. He'll find out for himself. He would sooner walk into fire than go home with his search unfinished. He stands and walks on, and the two men go home slowly, the poem says, looking back. Udayin argued from pleasure. These two argue from love, and then from doubt. And to doubt, the prince doesn't answer with a certainty of his own. He answers with a search.
screen: `THE HEART: YOUR FAMILY GRIEVES.` · `THE HEAD: PRACTICE AT HOME.` · `THE DOUBT: WHO REALLY KNOWS?` · `HE LISTENS, AND WALKS ON.` · then, large: `EVERY ARGUMENT.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a time someone pushed you hard to change your mind, and notice where the pressure shows up in your body, the jaw, the shoulders, the chest; breathe into that place. Then picture yourself the way the prince sits under the tree, hearing each point, not raising your voice, not folding. Let your feet press into the floor, and feel how steady the ground stays under all that talk.
doubt. What the king's minister raises against the prince's leaving, since no one can prove what comes after death; the prince answers not with certainty, but with a search. Today's word.
Your line: every argument. If no one can settle it, he'll go and look. Day seven hundred ten.

howItsDone: Buddhist communities teach the prince's resolve in this scene as an example of determination, and in some communities the story of family members asking a renunciant to come home is part of how people talk about ordination and the families of monks and nuns.

fork.reveal: he says he knows his father's love, that parting comes anyway, and that he won't settle the deepest question secondhand. he'd sooner walk into fire than go home unfinished.

trapdoor: what you thought: the ministers just begged him to come home.
what it means: they argue from love, from duty, from the example of old kings, and finally from doubt about any life after this.
what a scholar hears: the minister's speech gives voice to views of other schools of the time, such as that things happen by their own nature, so the prince's reply answers them, not only his family.
recall: a view or opinion someone holds

chat.says: When the minister said no one knows what comes after death, what did the prince do?

chat.meaning: He won't take the question secondhand from whoever sounds surest. He answers doubt with a search, not a certainty.

Udayin.meaning: the friend who argued for pleasure in the garden

family priest.meaning: the priest who served the royal household

forest.meaning: in these stories, where seekers go to live the holy life

notes: All Buddhacarita material paraphrased (Cowell 1894 is not on the validator list).

Confirm in Cowell canto 9: the envoys are the family priest (purohita) and the minister; where they find him (the script says only 'under a tree'); the appeal to ancestral kings who reached liberation while ruling; the advice to go to the forest in old age.

Confirm the minister's argument from doubt about the other world and from svabhava (things happen by their own nature; the sharpness of the thorn), and the prince's reply that he won't accept a doubtful view from others and would rather enter fire than return with his purpose unfulfilled.
Confirm 'the two men go home slowly, looking back' at the end of the canto.
Trapdoor floor 3: identifying the minister's views with other schools of the time is a scholarly reading; confirm it is fair.
howItsDone is general; confirm or simplify.

Auditor: 'the old kings of your line' made 'kings of old' (the priest's examples, e.g. Janaka, are not all of the prince's line); 'the prince listens to all of it' rewritten so he answers the priest and then the minister in turn, as the canto runs; myth reveal's leftover 'chief minister' made 'minister'.

Editor: 'two of the wisest people at court' and 'chief' cut (superlative); 'the most important question' cut; teach ending, practice sentence and carry rewritten because they repeated day 704's angle (hear the friend out, answer gently, 'I hear you') and day 708's 'doesn't call them fools'; the new ending points to the answer to doubt: a search.
